comment: The one definition of what looks like a secret in text read off the screen, for every platform's helper (ADR-DESK-046). The shared Rust core reads this file directly; every helper links it and passes redaction-cases.json through it.

Each redactor is data for one of a few shapes (kind), and one scanner reads them all. Every redactor looks at the text as read, never at what another found or took, so their order does not matter (owner, 2026-10-08): everything any of them takes goes, and one {placeholder} stands for each run of taken text that overlaps or meets. Every place a prefix, label or header occurs is looked at on its own; nothing a redactor finds hides the next place from it.
Character sets are written as in a bracket expression without the brackets: A-Z is a range, and a - at either end is itself. Lengths count characters.

edge "word": the prefix must not follow a letter, a digit or _ in the same piece of text, as ordinary words hold these prefixes (risk-..., pallbearer, benchmark_test_...). A prefix at the start of a piece the screen read shows on its own (a link, a bold run) has its edge, and so does one that starts inside or right at the end of text another redactor takes (a key glued to a key). A key of these kinds glued to the word before it in one piece stays shown: owner, 2026-10-08.
Every scanner takes time in proportion to the text, whatever the text; the Rust hostile-text timing test is authoritative.

redactors.name: private-key
redactors.description: A private key: from its header (-----BEGIN ... PRIVATE KEY-----) to its end line (-----END ... PRIVATE KEY-----). A header with no end line after it (a key cut off) takes the words of base64 after it (body, and an escaped line break's backslash) up to the first other character that is not whitespace; an end line with no header before it takes the text back to the start, or to just after the end line before it (owner, 2026-10-08), even other text read before the key. Only PRIVATE KEY lines count: a certificate's or a signature's lines take nothing.
redactors.label: PRIVATE KEY

redactors.name: key-lines
redactors.description: A key's body without its header or end line, wherever it is: two or more full lines of base64 (a label, a quote mark or a gutter may come before each), single base64 words between them, the line before them when it is the first line of the text and one base64 word (a text starting part-way through a key), and the first base64 word of the line after them, whatever follows it (owner, 2026-10-08), after the same kind of prefix as the lines had. Blank lines between them count as nothing. Other runs of such lines (a list of hashes, a base64 blob) go too (owner, 2026-10-05).

redactors.name: json-web-token
redactors.description: A JSON web token: base64url parts joined by dots, the second starting eyJ. A part starting eyJ after a dot, with a part after it, goes with the dot before it and the part after it, and with the part before it when that part holds eyJ (from there), so a token glued to another, or a third part starting eyJ, goes whole.

redactors.name: bearer-token
redactors.description: "Bearer <token>", as an Authorization header has it. The word and the space after it stay.

redactors.name: address-password
redactors.description: The password in an address (scheme://user:password@host), up to its last @. The rest stays.

redactors.name: named-value
redactors.description: A value given to a name that says it is secret (password=, api_key:, "token": "..."). The name stays. Only a value with a digit (0-9) in its first 201 characters and at least 6 characters, so that "Password: required" stays. Names match whatever their case (Unicode simple case folding).

redactors.name: payment-key
redactors.description: Live payment provider keys (secret, restricted, publishable).

redactors.name: payment-test-key
redactors.description: Test payment provider keys (secret, restricted, publishable).

redactors.name: aws-access-key-id
redactors.description: AWS access key ids: exactly 16 characters after the prefix; a word glued after it stays.

redactors.name: google-api-key
redactors.description: Google API keys: exactly 35 characters after the prefix; a word glued after it stays.

redactors.name: random-word
redactors.description: A word that looks random, whatever its prefix (owner, 2026-10-08): a run of word characters (padding at its end) is cut at each separator piece that is itself word-like, and a part goes when it is at least minLength long, holds a letter and a digit, is not hex (letters or a 0x before hex count as hex, so git hashes, digests, ids and hex numbers stay), is not an internationalized domain name's label (xn--), has at most maxWordShare of its characters in word-like runs (a capital and 3 or more small letters, 3 or more small letters, 3 or more capitals, or a number of 3 or more digits, so a media file's 3840x2160_60fps stays; a number cuts no word), and has at least minBits bits of Shannon entropy per character. Tuned on our own sources (no ordinary path, address, identifier or branch name goes) against random keys; see ADR-DESK-046.
